faq.q: What is the best free iOS app for motorcycle riding in the UK?
faq.a:
For an all-in-one free option we recommend VisorUp. It combines a custom route builder, live ride mode with turn-by-turn navigation, automatic fuel stops from 9,913 UK stations, 1,889 curated motorcycle-friendly points of interest, a weather overlay and GPX export, all with no ads. Because it is built specifically for UK touring, it covers British roads and stops in far more detail than a general navigation app.

You can download it free from the App Store.

faq.q: Will running navigation apps damage my iPhone on a motorcycle?
faq.a: It can. Apple has warned that high-amplitude engine vibration, particularly from larger-capacity bikes, can degrade the optical image stabilisation in an iPhone camera over time. The fix is simple: fit a vibration-dampening mount rather than a rigid clamp, and route power through a wired supply so the phone is held securely and charged. Many riders keep an older phone purely as a bike device.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for apps to navigate properly?
faq.a: No. Free apps such as VisorUp, Apple Maps and the Met Office cover the essentials well. Paid apps like OS Maps (around £24 a year) add unrivalled rural detail, and Kurviger Premium adds offline curvy-road routing. A sensible free-first setup is VisorUp for touring routes and live ride mode, Apple Maps for finding services, and the Met Office for weather.

faq.q: How do I stop notifications distracting me while riding?
faq.a: Set up a Focus mode on iOS. Go to Settings, then Focus, and create a Driving or custom riding Focus that silences everything except your chosen navigation app and calls from a safety contact. You can trigger it automatically when connected to your bike's Bluetooth intercom, so it turns on the moment you set off and off again when you stop.

faq.q: Which apps work offline for UK touring?
faq.a: VisorUp caches your route for offline use, and OS Maps, Apple Maps and Kurviger all let you download map areas in advance. This matters because mobile signal is patchy or absent across most of the Scottish Highlands, mid-Wales and the Pennines. Always download the whole area you are touring, not just a thin corridor along your planned route, in case you divert.

content:
Why Your iPhone Is a Rider's Best Tool

A modern iPhone, set up correctly, is the single most versatile piece of touring kit you can carry. It plans your route, navigates turn by turn, watches the weather, finds fuel, records your ride and calls for help if the worst happens. The trick is choosing the right apps and mounting the phone so it survives a day of engine vibration and British weather. This guide rounds up the best iOS apps for motorcycle riding in the UK for 2026, grouped by what they do, and explains the iPhone-specific settings that make them work properly on the bike.

Before we start, two hardware notes that matter more than any app. First, use a vibration-dampening mount, not a rigid clamp, because sustained engine vibration can damage an iPhone's camera stabilisation. Second, wire in a power supply, because running GPS with the screen on will flatten a battery in a few hours. Get those right and everything below just works.

All-in-One Touring: VisorUp

If you only install one app, make it VisorUp. It is a free, ad-free iOS app built specifically for touring Britain, and it folds most of the jobs below into a single, rider-focused interface. The route builder lets you drag and drop waypoints, choose a road preference between fast, curvy or twisty, and drop in automatic fuel stops roughly every 100 miles from a database of 9,913 UK fuel stations. When you set off, Live Ride Mode gives you GPS tracking, turn-by-turn directions, speed and ETA, optional voice navigation and automatic rerouting if you miss a turn.

Beyond navigation, VisorUp lets you explore 1,889 curated points of interest, the cafes, viewpoints, passes and castles that make a ride worth doing, and add any of them to your route with one tap. There is a weather overlay for planning, multi-day trip planning with day breaks, a packing checklist so you never leave the disc lock at home, and GPX export so you can share routes with friends over WhatsApp, email or AirDrop. It is genuinely free with no adverts, which is rare in this category. For a broader, platform-agnostic look at touring apps, our guide to the best apps for UK motorcycle touring is a useful companion.

Navigation

Navigation is where iOS shines, and you have real choice. Apple Maps has improved enormously and pairs seamlessly with CarPlay-equipped bikes and many aftermarket displays. Google Maps remains the best for finding services and checking opening hours. For riders who care about the journey rather than the destination, Kurviger and Calimoto actively seek out twisty roads and avoid motorways, while OS Maps provides Ordnance Survey detail no other app matches for rural Britain. VisorUp covers the touring-specific side with its route builder and live ride mode. We compare these in depth in our guide to the best iPhone motorcycle navigation apps.

Weather

UK weather can turn a great ride into a grim one, so a good forecast app is essential. The Met Office app is the most accurate for Britain, with hour-by-hour forecasts, weather warnings and a rain radar. Windy is brilliant for watching approaching systems visually and deciding whether to ride now or wait an hour. Yr.no from the Norwegian weather service is surprisingly good for mountain and coastal areas. Check the forecast the night before and again over breakfast, and use the radar to time your departure around showers.

Fuel and Services

Running low in the Highlands is no joke. PetrolPrices finds the cheapest and nearest fuel with opening hours, and VisorUp plans fuel stops into your route automatically so you never have to guess. For traffic and hazard reports on the busier approaches to touring country, Waze uses live community data to route you around jams.

Safety and Emergencies

What3Words divides the world into three-metre squares, each with a unique three-word address, and it is used by UK emergency services. If you come off in the middle of nowhere, it tells rescuers exactly where you are. Combine it with iOS features such as Emergency SOS and Medical ID, and share your live location with a safety contact through Find My or Apple Maps. An Apple Watch adds fall detection and hands-free Emergency SOS, which is a genuine safety net for solo riders. For a wider view of ride recording and safety tools, see our guide to the best iOS apps for motorcycle trip planning and ride tracking.

Communication

For group rides, a WhatsApp group is the simplest way to share locations and regroup at stops. If you run a Bluetooth intercom, the Cardo or Sena companion app handles pairing, settings and firmware updates. Pair your intercom with your chosen navigation app so you hear turn prompts without taking your eyes off the road.

iPhone Settings Every Rider Should Change

  • Focus mode: Create a riding Focus that silences everything except navigation and a safety contact, and trigger it automatically from your intercom's Bluetooth connection.
  • Offline data: Download maps and cache your route before you leave. Signal is unreliable across most touring areas.
  • Auto-Lock: Set the screen to never sleep while navigating, or rely on your app's own always-on mode, so directions stay visible.
  • Battery: Wire in power. GPS plus a bright screen drains a phone fast, and cold weather makes it worse.
  • Medical ID and Emergency SOS: Fill in your Medical ID and test Emergency SOS so first responders can access vital information.

Building Your iOS Riding Setup

You do not need a screen full of apps. A lean, reliable setup beats a cluttered one every time. Start with VisorUp for route planning and live navigation, add OS Maps for rural detail, the Met Office for weather, PetrolPrices for fuel and What3Words for emergencies. Install everything, test it at home, download your offline data, and set your riding Focus. Do that once and your iPhone turns from a distraction into the most useful tool on the bike, every mile of every ride.
